THREAD

THREAD (Trait Heterogeneity Regression through Expression Annotation and Dirichlet processes) integrates LD-corrected gene-level GWAS responses with gene-by-cellular-label expression profiles. Its heteroscedastic Bayesian nonparametric model infers latent gene modules and module-specific cellular coefficients.

Analyses can begin with raw GWAS and single-cell data or with prepared SNP-to-gene mappings, gene-level responses, or model inputs.

Main capabilities

  • Preprocess GWAS summaries and aggregate single-cell expression into a gene-by-cellular-label matrix.
  • Map SNPs to genes and construct LD-corrected gene-level responses with heteroscedastic uncertainty.
  • Infer latent gene modules and module-specific cellular coefficients with a Dirichlet process mixture.
  • Assess module-cellular-label associations using frequentist and Bayesian criteria.
  • Produce downstream gene and cellular-label prioritization scores.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub and load the package:

remotes::install_github("Jiacheng-Lou/THREAD", build_vignettes = TRUE)
library(THREAD)

Quick start

The installed example data demonstrate the interface only; they do not support biological conclusions. This example prepares model input from an expression matrix and a gene-level response:

library(THREAD)

example_dir <- system.file(
  "extdata", "example", package = "THREAD", mustWork = TRUE
)
example_X <- readRDS(file.path(example_dir, "example_x.rds"))
example_response <- readRDS(file.path(example_dir, "example_response.rds"))

thread_data <- prepare_input(
  X = example_X,
  response = example_response,
  K_init = 3L,
  min_genes = 10L,
  seed = 2028L,
  verbose = TRUE
)

See Getting Started for fitting, partitioning, association inference, and scores.

Full genome-wide LD reference data are not bundled with THREAD. Workflows that compute gene-level responses require a compatible external LD reference; see the response and input-format articles for details.

Citation

To obtain the current package citation, run:

citation("THREAD")
